content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free pasta is made from alternative grains and legumes such as rice, corn, buckwheat or lentils. It is suitable for people with celiac disease and anyone avoiding gluten. The taste and texture are close to traditional wheat pasta, and it cooks in the same way.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free pasta can be completely grain‑free when made from ingredients like konjac or legumes.
Many brands fortify it with B‑vitamins and iron to compensate for nutrients often lacking in a gluten‑free diet.
There are over 30 varieties of gluten‑free pasta, including spaghetti, penne and Asian‑style noodles.
Some manufacturers use double‑extrusion technology to improve texture and reduce stickiness.
Gluten‑free pasta usually has a lighter color compared with wheat pasta.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Being free of gluten, it is easier on the gut for those with sensitivity, reducing the risk of intestinal irritation.

items.title: Low allergen profile
items.content: Most varieties do not contain nuts, soy or dairy, making them safe for a wide range of consumers.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Provides a steady release of energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Pasta made from whole legumes or whole‑grain rice supplies dietary fiber that promotes gut health.

items.title: Vitamin profile
items.content: Fortified options can deliver iron, folate and B‑vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Allergy to alternative ingredients
items.content: Some gluten‑free pastas contain corn, soy protein or dairy starch, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Higher sodium content
items.content: Ready‑to‑cook gluten‑free mixes are sometimes salted for flavor; check the label.

items.title: Lower protein levels
items.content: Compared with wheat pasta, certain gluten‑free versions may provide less plant protein.

items.title: Texture quirks
items.content: Gluten‑free pasta can become overly soft or gummy if overcooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook gluten‑free pasta in plenty of salted boiling water for 7–12 minutes, depending on shape. Serve with classic sauces, vegetables, seafood, or in cold salads. For a firmer bite, toss with a little olive oil after draining.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry gluten‑free pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Once cooked, cool it quickly and refrigerate, using within 3 days.
